title: Riverbend Patient Financial Services Policy: Re-aging and Reinstating a Patient Payment Plan
content:
**1. When a re-age is available.** A representative may re-age a past-due **Patient Payment Plan** at the patient's request when the plan has been re-aged fewer times than the tier's re-age limit and at least the tier's minimum number of installments have been paid on it. Installments paid are counted over the life of the plan up to the day of the decision, as the installment payments numbered 1 or more on the plan (the down payment, numbered 0, is not counted).

**2. What a re-age moves.** The clause "A re-age moves the missed installments to the end of the schedule (re-age method): the installment amount is unchanged and the number of scheduled installments grows by the number of missed installments" is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis.

**3. Reinstatement window.** A defaulted plan may be reinstated only within the reinstatement window counted from the default date. The clock starts from the plan's default date as shown on the plan record. Count calendar days starting the day after the default date; a reinstatement on the last day of the window is accepted. The window length is the tier's reinstatement window.

**4. Reinstatement conditions.** Reinstatement also requires a catch-up payment of the tier's catch-up percentage of the missed amount (missed installments times the installment, rounded half-up to the cent) and that fewer reinstatements have been used than the tier allows; the rest of the missed amount moves to the end of the schedule.

**5. Outside these limits.** Outside these limits the patient's remaining balance stays on standard statements and a new plan may be requested only after the defaulted balances are brought current.

### Re-age availability (clause 1), hypothetical tier with a limit of 1 re-age and 2 installments paid

| Re-ages already used | Installments numbered 1 or more paid | Re-age available |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 2 | Yes |
| 0 | 1 | No |
| 1 | 4 | No |

### Reinstatement window (clause 3), hypothetical 30-day window

A plan defaulting on day D: a reinstatement on the 30th calendar day after D is accepted; one on the 31st day after D is outside the window.

### Catch-up (clause 4), hypothetical

Three missed installments of 80.00 make a missed amount of 240.00. At a 50 percent catch-up the payment required is 120.00, and the other 120.00 moves to the end of the schedule; at 100 percent the payment required is 240.00.

superseded_clauses: A re-age moves the missed installments to the end of the schedule (reage_method): the installment amount is unchanged and term_months grows by the number of missed installments.
